newsitem.title: USA: LecTec new drug application gets nod.
newsitem.headline: LecTec new drug application gets nod.

text.p: LecTec Corp said Monday the Food and Drug Administration approved its investigational new drug application for its cotinine-based smoking cessation pill.
As a result, the company may proceed with its next round of clinical testing and evaluation of its non-nicotine product.
Unlike other smoking cessation products currently on the market, including patches and gums, LecTec's product does not rely upon nicotine to ease smoking withdrawal symptoms.
The company's preliminary clinical evaluations have found cotinine, a natural metabolite of nicotine, to be safe and non-addictive.

In another recent development, the U.S. Patent Office has allowed a second patent covering the therapeutic claims that cotinine is a pharmaceutical useful for helping people stop smoking, maintain tobacco abstinence and alleviate abstinence-related tobacco craving.
LecTec is a medical company that develops, manufactures and markets products based on its advanced skin patch technologies, encompassing conductive hydrogels and adhesive coating.
